title: Infrared Absorption Spectroscopy of a Single Polyatomic Molecular Ion via Quantum Logic
author: Zhenlin Wu et al. / Philipp Schindler group, University of Innsbruck
key_claims: Quantum logic spectroscopy enables non-destructive IR absorption measurement of a single CaOH+ molecular ion
Schrödinger's cat entangled state between molecular ion and auxiliary atomic ion amplifies imperceptible photon recoil into measurable signal
O-H stretching vibration spectrum of singly-charged calcium hydroxide matches theoretical predictions from University of Warsaw collaborators
Method is generalizable to diverse molecular species for quantum-state preparation and precision spectroscopy
methodology: Trapped two-ion mixed-species crystal; quantum logic operations; entangled cat-state detection of single-photon recoil; comparison with ab initio theory
key_risk: None significant. Method validated against theory. Generalizability to larger polyatomic molecules remains to be demonstrated.
next_experiment: Extend to larger astrophysically relevant molecules (e.g., PAHs, metal hydrides) for laboratory astrochemistry; integrate with QPilotos quantum bridge for automated ion-trap control
notes: Landmark L1 result. Directly connects to C9 Quantum Bridge v2.0 (ion-trap backends) and Cluster 3 (quantum information). The 'cat-state amplification' principle mirrors the signal-boost logic used in C9 SNN focality metrics.
